Definition: feminine from G5015; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition:--trouble(-ing).
BiblicalUsage: The word is the troubling of the water, the stirring of the pool at Bethesda. An angel went down at a certain season into the pool and troubled the water, and whoever stepped in first after the troubling was made whole. The verse is found in the older Greek text; the newer text leaves it out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the troubled water shows how people waited on a stirring they could not command, and the Healer who came was greater than the pool.
